narrationScript: With our `index.html` file structured, let's now bring it to life with CSS. Create a new file named `styles.css` in the same directory. First, define a `font-family` for the entire `body` of the page to give it a consistent look. Next, center the text for your `<h1>` and `<h2>` elements. For your profile image, apply a `border-radius` to make it circular and add a `border` for a polished frame. Then, enhance your paragraph text by adding some `padding` for internal spacing and `margin` to separate it from other elements. Change the `color` of your list items to make them stand out. Finally, style your `<footer>` by giving it a distinct background color and centering its text. As you apply these styles, observe how the visual presentation of your profile page transforms. Experiment with different values to see their immediate impact. This exercise will solidify your understanding of how CSS selectors, properties, and values combine to control the aesthetics and layout of your web content.
